explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly compares LLM-as-a-judge results with human evaluation using human labels as ground truth, reports quantitative performance metrics (F1 scores), and discusses alignment between LLM probes and human raters

prompts.notes: General prompt template provided for pairwise comparisons and contrast pair harvesting. Full prompt templates available in Appendix E and code repository.

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: panel of human judges reached 80% agreement

guidelines.notes: Evaluation criteria descriptions provided (Table 3) but detailed annotation instructions not specified

sample_size.notes: Supervised probes trained on 5000 examples; human labels serve as ground truth for validation

quantitative_scores.notes: Both supervised and unsupervised probes achieve roughly F1=0.8 on MT-Bench with human majority-vote as ground truth

validation_results.summary_finding: Both supervised and unsupervised probes consistently outperform generation-based methods in aligning with human judgments, with F1 scores around 0.8 on MT-Bench and similar performance across diverse datasets and model families.

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM and human evaluate identical criteria across all evaluation tasks; human labels serve as ground truth for LLM validation
